newsitem.title: USA: Window blind cords strangle hundreds of children.
newsitem.headline: Window blind cords strangle hundreds of children.

text.p: A study released on Tuesday issued another warning to parents: keep the cords used to adjust window blinds away from toddlers.
At least 183 children, most of them three years of age or younger, were accidentally strangled in the cords between 1981 and 1995, the study said.

The study, which appeared in the Journal of the American Medical Association, said many of these strangulation deaths go unreported, and estimated that one such fatality occurs every two weeks in the United States.

"Any household furniture providing height near a window should be moved once a toddler is able to stand while holding onto furniture. Window cords should always be kept out of the reach of children," study authors Renae Rauchschwalbe of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and N. Clay Mann of Oregon Health Sciences University in Portland wrote.
"Because of this study and the attention it generates, hundreds of young lives could be saved," Consumer Product Safety Commission Chairman Ann Brown said in a statement.

The accidents can occur when infants become entangled by pulling the cords into their cribs, or toddlers grasp at the strings while climbing near windows. In many cases, the parents were home at the time but the child was unable to cry out.
The authors also recommended removing the loop from two-cord blinds and adding tassels, or using tie-down devices.
